skill.name: scientific-brainstorming
skill.description: A structured research ideation partner for generating hypotheses, challenging assumptions, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and planning practical next steps.
skill.summary: Develop diverse scientific ideas and turn promising directions into testable next steps.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All three static detections are false positives caused by benign brainstorming guidance; none performs or requests system reconnaissance. The files contain research ideation instructions and reference material without executable, network, filesystem, credential, or prompt-injection behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - What if you did less but better?
- Methods are tools, not rigid procedures—adapt as needed
- Avoid jargon from fields outside the scientist's expertise unless explaining it clearly.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 63 asks whether a research approach could do less but better within SCAMPER's Eliminate method. It does not inspect or collect system information.
Line 323 advises adapting brainstorming methods instead of treating them as rigid procedures. It contains no system discovery request or operational instruction.
Line 182 is communication guidance to explain unfamiliar scientific jargon clearly. It neither requests system details nor directs reconnaissance activity.

content.value_statement: Research questions can stall when assumptions and options remain hidden. This skill structures collaborative ideation to produce hypotheses, connections, methods, and practical next steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides ideation through context gathering, divergent exploration, connection making, critical evaluation, and synthesis.
Generates diverse hypotheses, research directions, and experimental concepts from a stated scientific challenge.
Applies SCAMPER, Six Thinking Hats, morphological analysis, TRIZ, biomimicry, and other documented methods.
Challenges assumptions through reversal, scale shifting, constraint changes, and cross-domain analogies.
Compares promising ideas by strengths, obstacles, feasibility, and required evidence.
Summarizes insights into literature questions, pilot experiments, collaboration needs, and immediate next steps.
limitations: It does not search publications or verify whether an idea is novel.
It cannot establish empirical correctness, feasibility, safety, or ethical acceptability.
Results depend on the context, constraints, and domain details supplied by the user.
It does not replace domain experts, formal study design, or institutional approval.

use_cases.title: Expand a thesis direction
use_cases.description: Generate hypotheses, identify hidden assumptions, and define small tests for an early research question.

use_cases.title: Resolve an R&D constraint
use_cases.description: Use structured methods to explore alternatives when cost, sensitivity, speed, or available equipment limits progress.

use_cases.title: Connect multiple disciplines
use_cases.description: Surface useful analogies, compatible methods, and collaboration opportunities across different scientific fields.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a research topic
prompt_templates.prompt: I study [topic] and want new research directions. Ask three context questions, then propose ten diverse ideas and group them by theme.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner exploration of a broad topic

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a project plan
prompt_templates.prompt: My project examines [question] using [method], with [constraints]. Challenge three assumptions, generate alternatives, and identify the smallest test for each promising idea.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing project

prompt_templates.title: Apply structured methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply SCAMPER and Six Thinking Hats to [research challenge]. Produce distinct options, compare strengths and risks, and recommend three directions for further investigation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured analysis of a defined challenge

prompt_templates.title: Map a complex opportunity space
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [complex research problem] with morphological analysis, TRIZ, biomimicry, and reverse assumptions. Identify novel combinations, contradictions, required evidence, and staged pilot experiments.

output_examples.input: Brainstorm low-cost methods to monitor pollinator activity across urban gardens.
output: Direction: Combine passive acoustic sensors with periodic visual counts to compare activity patterns.
Alternative: Recruit gardeners to collect standardized observations using fixed time windows.
First test: Compare both approaches at three sites before expanding the study.

output_examples.input: Challenge assumptions in a temperature-triggered drug delivery project.
output: Reversed assumption: Triggering may depend on local chemistry instead of temperature.
Scale shift: Test release behavior in microfluidic tissue models before whole-organism studies.
Key evidence: Measure off-target release, trigger stability, and delivery efficiency under realistic conditions.

output_examples.input: Find interdisciplinary approaches for studying misinformation spread.
output: Network science can model transmission paths and identify influential structures.
Epidemiology can suggest exposure, susceptibility, and intervention concepts for comparison.
Cognitive science can test how message framing changes acceptance and recall.

best_practices: Provide the research question, current model, available methods, constraints, and desired outcome.
Separate broad idea generation from later feasibility and evidence evaluation.
Verify promising directions with literature review, domain experts, and appropriately designed pilot studies.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated ideas as established findings or verified novelty.
Do not omit safety, ethics, statistical power, or regulatory review from later planning.
Do not request one preferred answer before exploring genuinely different alternatives.

faq.question: What scientific fields does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports broad scientific and engineering topics, especially when the user provides relevant domain context.

faq.question: Can it confirm that an idea is novel?
faq.answer: No. Novelty requires a current literature, patent, and prior-art review.

faq.question: Does it design complete experiments?
faq.answer: It can outline variables, comparisons, constraints, and pilot tests, but formal design requires domain and statistical review.

faq.question: Which brainstorming methods are included?
faq.answer: It includes SCAMPER, Six Thinking Hats, morphological analysis, TRIZ, biomimicry, provocation, random input, and assumption reversal.

faq.question: How should I evaluate the generated ideas?
faq.answer: Compare required evidence, feasibility, risks, resources, expected value, and the smallest informative test.

faq.question: Can teams use this skill together?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use its questions and structured methods to collect perspectives before selecting next steps.
